Keysight Technologies Inc reported revenue of $1.85 billion in the third quarter ended July 31, 2026, which represents a growth on a year earlier of 0.365385 according to [D1]. The company delivered net income of $531 million and earnings per share of $3.07 for the quarter based on non-GAAP measures as stated in [D1]. Orders surged 56% year-on-year to $2.09 billion, significantly exceeding market expectations and driven by demand for testing solutions linked to artificial intelligence infrastructure as noted in [D2]. The Communications Solutions Group emerged as the principal growth driver with commercial communications revenue jumping 56% while wireline revenue surpassed wireless revenue for the first time in the company's history according to [D3].

Management raised its outlook for the fourth fiscal quarter of 2026, expecting revenue in the range of $1.930 billion to $1.950 billion which is above the analyst consensus of $1.82 billion as reported in [D2]. Non-GAAP earnings per share are expected to be in the range of $3.34 to $3.40 compared with Wall Street expectations of approximately $2.68 per share according to [D2]. The company stated that supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue and that the supply environment is less flexible today than a year ago as argued by management in [D3]. Executives cautioned that one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 will not repeat, creating a high comparison bar for future profitability as mentioned in [D4].

Analysts have set price targets with a mean estimate of $418.42 indicating a potential upside of 30% from the current trading level as described in [D5]. The consensus price target comprises 12 short-term price targets with a standard deviation of $19.48 which helps understand the variability of the estimates according to [D5]. Strong agreement among analysts about the company's ability to report better earnings than they predicted earlier strengthens the view that the stock could gain as argued in [D5]. Several analysts have expressed skepticism regarding price targets, noting that business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts as stated in [D5].

The company announced participation in upcoming investor conferences including the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference on Friday, September 11, 2026 and the 2026 Truist Technology Symposium on Tuesday, September 15, 2026 as reported in [D6]. Keysight also announced a research collaboration with the Centre for Assuring Autonomy at the University of York to advance AI safety assurance for software-defined vehicles as detailed in [D7]. This collaboration focuses on developing practical methods for validating AI systems and generating evidence needed to demonstrate their safety and reliability according to [D7]. The research is expected to inform future development of Keysight's AI Software Integrity Builder and enable enhanced support for AI safety arguments as stated in [D7].
